rationale: The daily review-queue sweep (revalidate_review_queue, scheduled_tasks.review-queue-revalidate-daily, owner-approved 2026-08-06) cannot reach 38% of the work it is able to judge, and never will under its current selection. loadParkedReviewItems selects ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT max_items with NO item_type filter. The types with no revalidator return the 'unknown' verdict, which is deliberately NON-TERMINAL, so those rows stay parked, stay oldest, and are re-selected on every single run. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-06 before any change: 772 parked rows (status IN needs_human_review, unresolved); 168 in a type reviewRevalidators can judge; 396 of the oldest 500 unjudgeable; and 64 JUDGEABLE rows ranked beyond the 500-row head (required_fields_missing 48, needs_page 8, needs_section_data 7, unresolved_cta 1, oldest filed 2026-07-24). Only ~104 head slots ever turn over, so those 64 are not reached slowly, they are never reached. The first scheduled run measured the same thing from the other side: scanned 500, resolved 0, still_holds 31, unknown 469 - 94% of each pass is work that cannot possibly resolve, and each unjudgeable row also costs a real UPDATE (gate 2 stamps every judged item), so ~469 no-op writes per day re-stamping the same rows; 670 rows carry such a stamp today. Note the starved rows are the NEWEST covered ones, which inverts the selection's own stated rationale that 'the oldest items are the ones most likely to be describing a page state that no longer exists' - fresh findings are precisely the ones a recent re-render is likeliest to have already fixed. A cap raise (migration 321, 500->1500) is ALREADY APPLIED AND LIVE as a stopgap and un-starved all 64 today; this submission is the durable fix, because a cap sized to today's queue is consumed again by a backlog growing for unrelated reasons (parked rows accumulated 205 in the three days to 2026-08-06 against 55-81 in each prior week). The fix makes the cap bound JUDGEABLE work: filter the selection to the types reviewRevalidators actually covers, and report the coverage gap with one aggregate query instead of dragging ~600 unjudgeable rows through a per-row UPDATE. The filter is DERIVED from reviewRevalidators, so registering a revalidator widens the selection in the same edit and the two cannot drift.
submitter: bugfix_168_deployed_asset_path (retraction lane, picking up its own section 0 open item)

plan.summary: Make the review-queue sweep's cap bound judgeable work. Filter the selection to the item_types reviewRevalidators covers (derived from the map, so they cannot drift), refuse an operator-supplied uncovered type rather than returning a silent empty pass, count the coverage gap in full with one aggregate instead of accumulating whatever fell inside the cap, and warn when the cap binds so this can never again go unnoticed for a fortnight.

edits.rationale: The selection's source of truth, derived from reviewRevalidators so the filter and the registry CANNOT disagree - registering a revalidator widens what the sweep loads in the same edit, with nothing to remember. Sorted because Go map order is randomised per run, so an unsorted derivation reshuffles the generated IN list every pass, defeating plan caching and making the query unassertable in a test. Safe to interpolate through sqlInList (which does no escaping, by documented contract) because these are Go map keys - compile-time constants, never user input.

THE CORE CHANGE. Adds AND item_type IN (covered) to the selection so the cap bounds judgeable work and a backlog growing in an unrelated type can no longer push this sweep's own work out of the batch. The status list and the type list are interpolated from the same helpers, so gate 1 continues to match the two CAS gates.
edits.sketch:
query := fmt.Sprintf(`
	SELECT id::text, site_id, item_type, COALESCE(item_key, ''), COALESCE(spec, '{}'::jsonb)
	FROM site_work_items
	WHERE status IN (%s) AND item_type IN (%s)`,
	sqlInList(workItemRevalidatableStatuses), sqlInList(coveredItemTypes()))

edits.rationale: A NEW SILENT-FAILURE THE FILTER WOULD OTHERWISE CREATE, closed in the same change. Before the filter, an operator asking for an uncovered item_type got a batch of visibly useless 'unknown' stamps; after it, they would match no rows at all, and 'scanned 0' reads identically to 'the queue is drained'. So refuse, and name the covered set so the refusal is not a dead end. Pure (no DB) specifically so BOTH directions are unit-testable - the accept path is what stops a refusal that rejects everything from passing as correct.

Preserves the reporting the per-row 'unknown' path existed for (its comment: 'counted in uncovered_types, so the coverage gap is reported rather than silently read as nothing to drain') and makes it strictly better. The old shape reported only the uncovered rows that happened to fall INSIDE the cap, so the coverage gap looked SMALLEST exactly when the backlog was worst. One GROUP BY counts all of them. Scoped to the same statuses as the sweep or it would describe a different population. Read-only and explicitly not allowed to fail the pass: a broken count is a reporting problem, not a reason to stop draining.
edits.sketch:
SELECT item_type, count(*)
FROM site_work_items
WHERE status IN (<revalidatable>) AND item_type NOT IN (<covered>)
GROUP BY item_type
// caller: on error, log at WARN and continue with an empty map

edits.rationale: Wires the above and adds the signal whose absence let this sit for a fortnight. cap_binding (len(items) >= maxItems) is logged at WARN in the words of the consequence - judgeable rows were left unexamined - because the payload has always carried capped_at and nobody compares two numbers in a JSON blob nobody reads. The !covered branch is now unreachable by construction but is KEPT and made loud (logger.Error) because 'the filter and the registry agree' is the property the whole change rests on; if it ever fires they have drifted and the sweep is judging blind.

The header lists 'no revalidator for the type' as a cause of unknown. After this change that cause is unreachable, so an unknown always means a revalidator looked and could not tell. Leaving the header stale would make a reader believe uncovered types are still being stamped. Also records that uncovered_types CHANGED MEANING on this date - it now counts every parked unjudgeable row rather than the subset inside the cap - so anyone comparing runs across the date knows they are comparing two different measurements.

Four tests pinning the properties the safety argument rests on: the filter IS the registry (asserted equal to the map's sorted keys, stable across 8 calls, non-empty so it cannot match nothing); the filter is actually IN the selection (source scan, because the failure guarded against is a missed edit, not a wrong result); an uncovered type is refused with an actionable message; and EVERY covered type is still accepted, which is what stops a blanket refusal passing the previous test.

DELIBERATE UPDATE TO AN EXISTING GUARD, declared rather than quietly adjusted. The test asserts sqlInList(workItemRevalidatableStatuses) appears exactly 3 times (selection + 2 CAS guards). reportUncoveredBacklog is a fourth use and MUST carry the same status list or it would count a different population than the sweep drains. It is NOT a gate - it is read-only, so it can misreport but cannot select-then-fail-to-update, which is the failure the other three share. Count goes to 4 with that distinction written into the failure message; the second assertion (no surviving literal 'status = needs_human_review') is untouched.

grounded_in: revalidate_review_queue_action.go:301 (pre-change): 'query += fmt.Sprintf(" ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT $%d", len(args))' - the selection had no item_type predicate at all.

reviewRevalidators' own comment: 'An item_type absent from this map yields unknown and is counted in uncovered_types, so the coverage gap is reported rather than silently read as "nothing to drain".' - the reporting intent this change preserves and widens.

loadParkedReviewItems' own comment: 'reads the queue, oldest first - the oldest items are the ones most likely to be describing a page state that no longer exists.' The starved rows are the NEWEST covered ones, so the effect inverts the stated rationale.
LIVE MEASUREMENT 2026-08-06, ranked by created_at over status IN (needs_human_review, unresolved): in_oldest_500=t/covered=t 104; t/f 396; f/t 64; f/f 215. The 64 are the finding.
LIVE MEASUREMENT 2026-08-06, the 64 by type: required_fields_missing 48 (oldest 2026-07-24), needs_page 8, needs_section_data 7, unresolved_cta 1.
First scheduled run, recorded in the lane handoff section 0: 'scanned 500 - resolved 0 - still_holds 31 - unknown 469 - dry_run false'.

applyRevalidation gate 2 runs for every non-resolved verdict including unknown, so each unjudgeable row costs one UPDATE per pass: 'UPDATE site_work_items SET result = COALESCE(result,'{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object('revalidation', $2::jsonb) WHERE id = $1::uuid AND status IN (...)'. Live count of rows carrying that stamp with verdict unknown: 670.

CONSUMER CHECK (owner ruling 2026-07-29 #3, tell them do not merely measure): grep over platform/, internal/, pkg/ for 'revalidation' and 'uncovered_types' finds NO reader outside this action - page_section_satisfiability.go produces verdicts, it does not consume stamps; the only other hit is a comment in review_queue_drain/seed_review_queue_revalidator.sql. Consumers named and being told: the review_queue_drain lane (owns the action, docs dormant since 2026-07-28), the bugs_open/187 lane (added the needs_page revalidator 2026-08-03), and scheduled_tasks.review-queue-revalidate-daily (behaviour changes: scanned drops to judgeable rows only, uncovered_types grows to the full backlog).

Stopgap already live and recorded: migration 321_review_queue_sweep_reaches_every_parked_row.sql, applied 2026-08-06 09:04 UTC, max_items 500->1500, guard asserted 0 covered rows beyond the cap afterwards. This submission is the durable fix, not a duplicate of it.
plan.risks: 1) BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, STATED PLAINLY: the sweep stops stamping result.revalidation on rows it cannot judge. That stamp carried no information beyond 'no revalidator registered for item_type X', no code reads it (grepped, see grounded_in), and the same fact is now reported in aggregate for ALL such rows rather than the subset inside the cap. The 670 existing stamps are left in place and untouched - this change neither writes nor removes them. 2) The payload key uncovered_types changes meaning on the same date (subset-inside-cap -> full backlog); it is now larger and it is the true figure. Recorded in the file header and the payload comment so a reader comparing runs across the date is not misled. Nothing consumes the key. 3) An operator passing an uncovered item_type now gets an ERROR where they previously got a useless-but-successful pass. This is the intended direction (a silent empty pass is indistinguishable from a drained queue) but it IS a contract change for a manual caller; the scheduled row supplies no item_type and is unaffected, and TestEveryCoveredTypeFilterIsAccepted pins that the blank-filter path still means 'all covered types'. 4) sqlInList does no escaping by documented contract; the values interpolated are Go map keys, compile-time constants, never operator input - the operator-supplied filter continues to go through a bound parameter. 5) The change cannot fix the underlying coverage gap - ~611 parked rows are still in types nothing revalidates. It stops that backlog stealing the cap from work that CAN be judged, and makes its true size visible every run; closing it means more revalidators, which is separate and per-type reviewable. 6) Inert until a chassis roll; the stopgap cap raise (migration 321) is what protects the queue in the meantime, and the two are safe in either order - the new binary reads a larger cap it no longer needs, the old binary reads a filter it does not have.
